reason: REFUTED on severity and on the fix; the underlying observation is only half right. Driven at 390/768/1280/1440 across all seven states: the seat's mechanical facts hold — twelve .colw are plain spans (anyTabbable false, anyTip false, anyTitle false), #count is a SPAN, and the fifteen focusables at 1440 are exactly three .tab links, three .kpi links and nine .dot buttons, tab order tabs > KPIs > dots. But the finding is factually wrong where it counts hardest: the sentence does not appear 'in any of the seven states' — it renders in four (full, partial, quiet, loading). first-run replaces the whole hero-note with 'Four weeks of records make a comparison worth printing…', and empty and error render no .hero-fig at all. Severity is overstated, and an overstated class refutes the finding. 'misleading' means the product asserts something untrue. The sentence's subject is 'each job', not this page: it says the 31 is a count of real job records rather than an aggregate estimate, and every one of those records is openable — in Tasks, which is true of the product. Nothing untrue is asserted. What is wrong is that the line invites an action this surface does not carry a door for — a copy/affordance mismatch, visibly wrong but passable, i.e. defect. It is also weaker than the seat implies given the surrounding convention: three .kpi cards are already <a href='#'> stubs going nowhere, so a dead destination is this prototype's established idiom, not evidence the screen is broken. The preferred fix is measurably wrong. Column width is 22.0px at 390 (43.5 at 768, 53.5 at 1280 and 1440); audit.mjs pushes any interactive element whose min(w,h) < 28 onto out.targets, so twelve .colw buttons fail the targets gate at 390 on the narrow axis, and the pseudo-element expander the gate honours cannot rescue it — the columns are flush neighbours, so widening one to 28 overlaps and steals the adjacent column's clicks. Worse, the proposed accessible name ends '— open them' on a control with no destination: that relocates the very defect being reported into the screen-reader layer, where a blind reader hears an explicit command and gets silence. It also adds twelve tab stops between the tab strip and the KPI row, tripling the keyboard path of a page whose job is reading, and the seat bundles in a claim that this closes twelve-columns-withhold-their-own-numbers, which is a data-legibility finding, not an affordance one.
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's own fallback branch, not its preferred one: delete the second sentence at lately.html:609 so the line reads 'Counted at the moment each job reached a done column.' That is the honest half — it is the provenance note the hero actually needs — it costs nothing, touches no gate, and removes the invitation without inventing a control. If and only if the port has a real destination, the affordance belongs on the numeral or on one explicit link beneath it ('Open these 31 in Tasks') — a single tab stop at full control size — never on twelve 22px-wide columns. Column readability is a separate problem with a separate fix: give the columns their values on hover/focus of the plot as a whole, or print the numbers, and let twelve-columns-withhold-their-own-numbers be judged on its own merits.
breaks: The sharpened fix (cutting one sentence) breaks nothing structural, but re-measure: the .hero-fig is a two-part stack and .hero-note is its second line, so removing it shortens the hero card and shifts the chart up — re-shoot light-full, light-partial, light-quiet and light-loading at 1440x960, and re-check the 390 stack where the hero-note wraps and currently sets the card's height. Re-run audit.mjs for leading/ramp (one fewer t-small instance changes the type-ramp counts) and interaction-check.mjs, which measures '.plot .colw:last-child .bar' bounding heights at lines 268/509/515 — those are viewport-relative and will move if the hero shrinks. If the seat's preferred fix were taken instead, re-measure targets at 390 (it fails there at 22x168), the full tab order at all four widths, the tip layer's collision with .record-tag and .bar-val inside .plot, and whether the tip overflows the card at 390.
